sense: a public show of art or objects

terms.comment: Levi and Bini’s word, from expōnere, which Pliny uses of pictures put on show in public (Plin. NH 35.52: in pūblicō expōnī). Classically expositiō is a setting forth in words, a narration (Cic. Or. 212), and also the exposing of an infant (Lewis & Short), so say what is on show when there is any doubt (see exhibit).

terms.gloss: a show, anything put on for people to see
evidence: Cic. Fin. 5.48: pompā, lūdīs atque ejus modī spectāculīs
terms.comment: The general classical word for a show: games, a procession, a play, a sight (see scene, a sight).

evidence: M-O s.v. museum (with a query, from Egger)
terms.comment: Classically the producing of a document or a person, and maintenance, support (Gell. 14.2.7; the Digest; Lewis & Short); expositiō says “exhibition” without the legal sense.

phrases.latin: Crās tabulās pictās quae in mūsēō prōpositae sunt vīsēmus.
phrases.english: Tomorrow we’ll go and see the pictures on show at the museum.

sources: Lewis & Short: expositio · Lewis & Short: expono · Lewis & Short: spectaculum · Lewis & Short: exhibitio
